messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: realtime alert — streaming.tail.p99 for tenant FathomAI exceeded SLO. p99=5.9s (SLO=2s) over 3m window. Rule=streaming_tail_p99 > 2s.

pagerduty: Paging ria

ria: I'm up, starting triage. Any immediate customer impact numbers (errors vs slow responses)?

sam: Graphs show p95 ~ 480ms, p99 spiking to 5.9s. Streaming stall rate jumped to ~14%. Concurrent sessions for FathomAI are ~280 (typical ~65). Lots of long-lived streams.

lee: Runtime logs: huge KV cache eviction bursts; top of heap churn correlated with the p99 window. Many requests share very long identical prefixes (~3.5k-5k tokens). Looks like a single-tenant prompt storm with high fanout.

julie: ModelOps: tenant is pinned to redwood-llama-ft-70b-q4 in their tenant config. We have llama-13b-q4/llama-7b-q4 fallbacks ready.

ria: Quick mitigation slate: 1) limit concurrency for tenant to 130 (queue new sessions) 2) enable 13b fallback for new sessions (canary then ramp) 3) enable routing-level prefix dedupe/grouping to reduce KV cache duplication 4) temporarily drop max_stream_chunk_size to reduce blocking I/O. Lee/Sam — please implement. Ashley will prepare the customer update.

lee: Applying concurrency cap now via router API:

```
POST /routes/tenants/fathomai/policies
{
  "policy_type":"concurrency_limit",
  "limit":130,
  "behavior":"queue"
}
```

lee: Concurrency cap in place. New sessions will be queued. Existing sessions unaffected.

sam: Kicking off model fallback rollout for new sessions — canary 20% -> observe -> 100% if stable. Command I used:

```
redwood rollout create --tenant fathomai --policy fallback:llama-13b-q4 --canary 20
```

sam: Canary live. Monitoring tail metrics.

matt: Infra can add capacity. Spinning up 3 extra GPU nodes to the Dedicated pool for that tenant (+~25% throughput). ETA ~4m. Also raising network eBPF counters to capture retransmits for the window.

sam: Also toggled prefix dedupe grouping on router (canary 10%) to collapse identical long prefixes to the same KV cache shard. Patch applied:

```
PATCH /tenants/fathomai/config
{"prefix_dedupe": {"enabled": true, "canary_pct": 10}}
```

sam: Lowered max_stream_chunk_size from 64KB -> 24KB for the tenant to limit head-of-line blocking on IO writes.

lee: Infra scale completed: +3 hosts added. KV eviction rate trending down. Queue size peaked ~85 then drained.

sam: After 6m of mitigations: p95=430ms, p99=2.1s, stall_rate=4.8%, active accepted sessions 124, queued 18. Canary fallback at 20% helped immediately.

sam: After prefix-dedupe ramp to 100% and full fallback ramp: p95 380ms, p99 1.6s, stall_rate 2.7%. Looks stable.

julie: Customer-quality note: 13b fallback reduces some fidelity on very long, specific prompts (especially transcription nuance). We can whitelist critical session IDs to keep on 70b if FathomAI requests it. Recommend we include that as an option in the customer comms.

ashley: Drafting message to FathomAI support channel: "We observed elevated streaming latencies for your tenant. We've applied traffic controls, a temporary model fallback, and routing-level prefix dedupe. Latency has returned within SLO; we'll monitor and follow up with a timeline and RCA." Adding estimated mitigation window 30-60m.

ria: Good. Make CS aware that fallback was applied as default for new sessions — existing sessions stayed on 70b. Also mention whitelist option.

lee: I'm collecting hot-prefix diagnostics and eviction timelines for RCA. Command used to export prefixes and eviction timestamps:

```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=runtime -c kvcache | grep "evict" | awk '{print $1,$6,$12}' > /tmp/fathomai_kv_evictions.log
```

sam: Increasing trace sampling for that tenant to catch streaming stalls — set to 1200 traces/min for 20m. Also exporting p95/p99 slices and stream traces to incident bundle.

matt: Noted a spike in TCP retransmits on one top-of-rack during the timeframe; it's a secondary signal, not the primary cause, but capturing it for RCA.

ashley: Customer replied: "Thanks for the heads-up. Can you confirm if any data left their VPC?" Answered: "No, no data exfiltration; this was performance-only, changes are routing/model fallbacks controlled on our side." They asked for periodic updates every 30m.

ria: Owners and post-incident plan: Runtime eng (lee + sam) — KV cache & batching; Infra (matt) — network + capacity dimension; ModelOps (julie) — fallback policy & quality tradeoffs; CS (ashley) — customer comms. Target postmortem draft in 48 hours, public facing summary for customer within 72 hours.

lee: Exporting dashboards + logs to incident archive: /incidents/5551234567/ (saved slices, traces, kvcache dumps).

pagerduty: Handoff to night oncall: sam (now oncall).

sam: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor and will escalate if p99 > 3s again.

ashley: Sent updated note to customer: "Latency within SLO; mitigations in place; RCA and next steps forthcoming." They acknowledged.

incbot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Associated ticket: INC-2026-5551234567

ria: Closing this thread for now. If anything regresses, page immediately. Thanks team."
